facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Notes payable tie, September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:13): 117,582 + 600,000 + 500,000 + 339,761 = 1,557,343, which equals the printed total notes payable of 1,557,343. Less unamortized debt issuance cost and discount of 17,712 gives 1,539,631, equal to the printed 1,539,631. 2. Total debt tie (page:13-14): 1,539,631 + finance lease obligations 94,721 = 1,634,352, equal to the printed total debt including current maturities. Balance sheet (page:2): 11,229 + 1,623,123 = 1,634,352. Ties. The revolver balance is nil at September 30, 2026 and 100,000 at December 31, 2025 (page:14). 3. December 31, 2025 notes tie (10-K page:112): 78,899 + 148,590 + 117,582 + 600,000 + 339,761 = 1,284,832, equal to the printed total. The 10-K principal repayable schedule (page:113: nil in 2026, 78.9 million in 2027, 148.6 million in 2028, 217.6 million in 2029, nil in 2030, 939.8 million thereafter, in dollars of millions) sums to 78.9 + 148.6 + 217.6 + 939.8 = 1,384.9 million dollars, versus 1,284.8 million dollars of notes plus the 100.0 million dollar revolver draw at that date = 1,384.8 million dollars; the 0.1 million dollar difference is rounding. The 10-K contractual obligations table prints 1,384.8 million dollars of debt excluding finance leases and interest (page:73). 4. Weighted-average coupon test for the 2042 notes (principal-weighted, on the four tranches outstanding at September 30, 2026; the release gives 6.3 percent, release 2026-11-04 page:2). Using 6.375%: (117,582 × 7.050 + 600,000 × 6.000 + 500,000 × 6.500 + 339,761 × 6.375) ÷ 1,557,343 = (828,953 + 3,600,000 + 3,250,000 + 2,165,976) ÷ 1,557,343 = 9,844,929 ÷ 1,557,343 = 6.32 percent, which rounds to 6.3. Using 5.875% for the 2042 notes: (828,953 + 3,600,000 + 3,250,000 + 1,996,096) ÷ 1,557,343 = 9,675,049 ÷ 1,557,343 = 6.21 percent, which rounds to 6.2. The release figure therefore matches the 6.375% label. This supports, but does not prove, that 6.375% is the current coupon; the cause of the change is not supplied. 5. Liquidity inputs (10-Q Q3 page:47; page:14): cash and cash equivalents 500.3 million dollars; Amended RCF commitment 2.0 billion dollars; borrowings nil; letters of credit 0.4 million dollars. Undrawn capacity net of letters of credit = 2,000.0 − 0.4 = 1,999.6 million dollars; plus cash 500.3 = 2,499.9 million dollars, consistent with "approximately 2.5 billion" and the release's 2.50 billion dollars. Not a liquidity analysis: no minimum cash, expiring facility or restricted cash review is done here. The cash figure includes NCI (release page:2) and 105.1 million dollars held outside the United States (10-Q Q3 page:47). 6. Perimeter bridge for Q3 2026 production (release 2026-11-04 page:13): 192,283 − 5,788 = 186,495 BOE per day, equal to the printed excluding-NCI figure. 7. Segment-to-statement difference for 2025 comparatives (10-Q Q3 page:29, page:30 versus page:3): three months, 733.2 − 732.985 = 0.2 million dollars; nine months, 2,096.7 − 2,094.266 = 2.4 million dollars (rounded to one decimal). 2026: 854.9 versus 854.974 and 2,516.8 versus 2,516.833, equal within rounding. 8. Net debt as printed by management (release 2026-11-04 page:10-11): total debt 1,634.3 − cash 500.3 = 1,134.0 million dollars at September 30, 2026; 1,385.0 − 377.2 = 1,007.8 million dollars at December 31, 2025. Both tie. This management measure includes the revolver draw at year-end 2025 and is stated including NCI cash.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is sufficient for a credit snapshot of MURPHY OIL CORP, with stated restrictions. Evidence: the audited FY2025 statements and the unaudited Q1 to Q3 2026 statements are complete and tie to the debt note (total debt 1,634.4 million dollars at September 30, 2026 equals current maturities of 11.229 plus long-term debt of 1,623.123 million dollars). Calculated EBITDA (operating income plus DD&A plus impairment, consolidated) is 1,837.5 million dollars for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 against 1,394.0 million dollars for FY2025, so total debt over EBITDA is 0.89x against 0.99x and net debt over EBITDA is 0.62x against 0.72x even though debt rose by 249.3 million dollars. Mechanism: revenue from production rose in the nine months (2,507.9 against 2,076.8 million dollars) on higher realized prices while ex-NCI volumes fell (176,620 against 182,585 BOEPD), and lease operating expenses fell from 605.0 to 436.4 million dollars; the 2025 comparison also carries a 115.0 million dollar impairment that the calculation adds back. Management's own ex-NCI adjusted EBITDA gives a close cross-check: 1,784.8 million dollars for the same twelve months, or 0.92x total debt. Source risk and consequence: the strength of the leverage and cover ratios rests on a high price period and a calculated, NCI-inclusive EBITDA; the free cash flow cushion is small because property additions and dry hole costs of 1,333.0 million dollars absorb most of the 1,517.6 million dollars of operating cash flow, and the balance sheet carries claims outside the debt figure (operating leases, asset retirement obligations, pension and retiree medical, commitments). The metrics therefore support a view of low financial leverage with good near-term liquidity and no note maturity until May 2029, but not a view of covenant headroom, instrument seniority or guarantor coverage, which the sources cannot verify.

The metrics therefore support a view of low financial leverage with good near-term liquidity and no note maturity until May 2029, but not a view of covenant headroom, instrument seniority or guarantor coverage, which the sources cannot verify.

facts.label: Definitions
facts.text: - EBITDA (calculated) = operating income from continuing operations + depreciation, depletion and amortization + impairment of assets. It is consolidated, includes NCI, excludes other income (loss) (which carries foreign exchange gains and losses) and keeps accretion of asset retirement obligations and exploration expenses as costs. EBITDAX = EBITDA + exploration expenses, including undeveloped lease amortization. These are not the management definitions, which start from net income attributable to Murphy, exclude NCI, add back accretion and remove foreign exchange and derivative items (EX-99.1 2026-11-04 page:9-10). - LTM Q3 2026 = FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025, applied to each flow line. - Total debt = total debt including current maturities (notes net of discount plus finance leases) plus the revolver draw. Net debt = total debt less cash and cash equivalents. - Free cash flow (calculated) = net cash provided by continuing operations activities less property additions and dry hole costs, without removing working capital changes and including NCI.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: MURPHY OIL CORP is an independent, publicly listed oil and gas exploration and production company with no sponsor, no controlling owner identified in the sources and no acquisition or leveraged transaction driving the credit view. The decision drivers are therefore the operating model and recent change, not transaction structure. Evidence: crude oil and condensate is 86.1 percent of nine-month 2026 revenue from production, no commodity derivative contracts were in place at September 30, 2026, and realized prices rose sharply on the year (for example United States onshore crude at 86.48 dollars per barrel in Q3 2026 against 65.48 dollars in Q3 2025) while total hydrocarbon production fell 7 percent in Q3 2026 and 3 percent in nine months 2026, which management attributes mainly to lower Gulf of America volumes (natural decline) and to the timing of new onshore wells (10-Q Q3 page:34-36). Risk mechanic: an oil-weighted, unhedged revenue base converts price moves almost directly into cash flow, so the 2026 earnings recovery is a price result with lower volumes; sustaining production requires continuing capital in decline-prone Gulf of America fields (about half of nine-month revenue is United States offshore) while the company also funds exploration and appraisal in Côte d'Ivoire, Vietnam and the Gulf of America. Credit implication: leverage and liquidity are currently strong (CP-1 handoff), but they depend on commodity prices and on management choosing to keep exploration and shareholder returns within cash flow; the sources show that discretion being exercised conservatively on buybacks and with a refinancing that extended maturities, but they do not show the covenant or indenture limits that would constrain distributions or new debt. Credit-relevant change in the period: the January 2026 refinancing (500.0 million dollars of 6.500% notes due 2034, 227.5 million dollars of 2027 and 2028 notes redeemed, revolver upsized to 2.0 billion dollars and extended to January 2031), the first oil at Lac Da Vang in Vietnam with an 83.9 million dollar finance lease for its floating storage vessel, raised 2026 production guidance, and an October 2026 drillship agreement worth approximately 225 million to 325 million dollars gross. The view is limited by missing ownership percentages, customer concentration and capital allocation plan terms (see Gaps).

Credit-relevant change in the period: the January 2026 refinancing (500.0 million dollars of 6.500% notes due 2034, 227.5 million dollars of 2027 and 2028 notes redeemed, revolver upsized to 2.0 billion dollars and extended to January 2031), the first oil at Lac Da Vang in Vietnam with an 83.9 million dollar finance lease for its floating storage vessel, raised 2026 production guidance, and an October 2026 drillship agreement worth approximately 225 million to 325 million dollars gross. The view is limited by missing ownership percentages, customer concentration and capital allocation plan terms (see Gaps).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: MURPHY OIL CORP is a financially conservative but price-exposed oil producer, and its credit is sound today. The strongest support is low leverage (total debt of USD 1,634.4 million is 0.89x calculated last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million), liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million and no note maturing before May 2029. The weakest point is that crude oil supplies 86.1 percent of revenue with no commodity derivatives in place, while exploration, development and a new drillship commitment absorb most operating cash flow, leaving little after dividends. What decides the outcome is the oil price and management's willingness to cut discretionary spending and buybacks when it falls; the covenant and indenture limits that would bound that discretion are not in the sources.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the company's leverage is low and has fallen even though debt rose. Total debt was USD 1,385.1 million at December 31, 2025 and USD 1,634.4 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 249.3 million from a USD 500.0 million notes issue, a USD 83.9 million finance lease and the repayment of USD 227.5 million of notes and the USD 100.0 million revolver draw, while calculated EBITDA rose from USD 1,394.0 million (FY2025) to USD 1,837.5 million (LTM Q3 2026), so total debt over EBITDA moved from 0.99x to 0.89x [CP-1 Debt stack; Chart data: leverage]. The management-basis cross-check gives 0.92x on adjusted EBITDA attributable to Murphy of USD 1,784.8 million.

facts.text: Weaknesses. Unhedged oil exposure: crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and no commodity derivatives were in place at September 30, 2026; a 10 percent lower oil price on nine-month volumes would have cut revenue and EBITDA by about USD 215.9 million, or 14.0 percent of nine-month calculated EBITDA, before any cost offset (Documentary Fact for the exposure, Analyst Interpretation for the arithmetic) [CP-1A Hedging; Revenue streams]. Thin cash cushion after investment and dividends, as described above (Documentary Fact for the amounts) [CP-1 Free cash flow]. Concentration and decline: United States offshore supplies 50.2 percent of nine-month revenue, and production including the minority share fell 7 percent in Q3 2026, mostly on Gulf of America volumes (Documentary Fact for the percentages, Management Language for the cause) [CP-1A Geographic revenue mix; Volume and mix]. Discretionary, high-risk spending: exploration expense was USD 155.2 million for nine months 2026, including USD 86.7 million of unsuccessful well costs, and the drillship agreement adds a contracted element from 2027 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Cost structure; Transaction summary]. Claims outside debt, including asset retirement obligations equal to about 65 percent of total debt (Analyst Interpretation, calculated) [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Unverified creditor terms: covenants, indentures, ratings, ownership percentages and customer concentration are missing (Insufficient Information; each missing datapoint is listed under Gaps) [CP-0 Gaps; CP-1A Gaps]. Perimeter: the minority holder takes a share of Gulf of America cash flow, 13.5 percent of consolidated nine-month 2026 net income, and releases and filings use different perimeters (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model: MP GOM subsidiary].

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Illustrative oil price sensitivity (arithmetic, not a forecast): nine-month 2026 crude oil and condensate revenue of USD 2,158.6 million (CP-1A, from 10-Q Q3 page:8-9) times 10 percent = USD 215.9 million; divided by nine-month 2026 calculated EBITDA of USD 1,537.3 million = 14.0 percent. It assumes constant volumes, no cost or royalty offset and no tax effect. 2. Mechanical distance to the previous facility's stated levels (not covenant headroom): total debt USD 1,634.4 million divided by 3.25 = USD 502.9 million, so calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million could fall by 72.6 percent before total debt over EBITDA reached 3.25x; interest paid of USD 86.3 million times 2.50 = USD 215.8 million, so EBITDA could fall by 88.3 percent before EBITDA over interest paid reached 2.50x. The covenant definitions are not supplied. 3. Claims-inclusive leverage (illustrative): total debt USD 1,634.352 million + operating lease liabilities USD 653.756 million (September 30, 2026) + asset retirement obligations USD 1,065.394 million (September 30, 2026) + pension and retiree medical net liabilities USD 195.814 million (USD 132.415 million + USD 63.399 million, December 31, 2025) = USD 3,549.316 million; divided by USD 1,837.474 million = 1.93x. It mixes dates, treats asset retirement obligations as debt-like although they are costs of operations, and excludes commitments and letters of credit. Asset retirement obligations over total debt: 1,065.394 / 1,634.352 = 65.2 percent. 4. Cash walk, nine months 2026 (USD million, 10-Q Q3 page:4-5): operating cash flow 1,517.609 - investing outflow 1,361.686 = 155.923; less financing outflow 32.834, plus exchange effect 0.016 = 123.105, equal to the increase in cash from 377.196 to 500.301. 5. Free cash flow after distributions, nine months 2026 (CP-1): 184.570 - 150.528 - 21.164 = 12.878, shown as USD 12.9 million. 6. Interest cost sensitivity of the 2042 notes coupon: 339.761 million times 0.5 percentage points = USD 1.7 million a year (1,698.8 thousand). 7. Figures carried unchanged from CP-1 and CP-1A, recomputed here as a check: total debt 1,634.352 / EBITDA 1,837.474 = 0.89x; net debt 1,134.051 / 1,837.474 = 0.62x; EBITDA 1,837.474 / interest paid 86.305 = 21.29x; liquidity 500.301 + 1,999.6 = 2,499.9; operating cash flow growth 1,517.609 / 998.162 - 1 = 52.0 percent. All match.

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: MURPHY OIL CORP (issuer id mur; ticker MUR; registrant name in the filings "Murphy Oil Corporation", Delaware, file number 1-8590). As-of date and cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot, run type research, public case. Current period q3-2026 (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026); prior period fy-2025 (year ended December 31, 2025). Reporting currency: USD. The financial statements are stated in thousands of US dollars; narrative, segment and non-GAAP tables are in millions; no other reporting currency is used by the issuer, although Canadian operations are translated and the Canadian fixed-price gas forward sales are priced in C$ (EX-99.1 2026-11-04 page:14).

Question for this module: can the seven pinned sources support the requested minimum module set (CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5), and what remains blocked or limited? This module gives source readiness only: no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation, no investment opinion. Figures below are quoted from the sources to locate evidence and to test consistency between sources; none is normalized or offered as an analytical result.

Perimeter: the reporting entity is the parent registrant, Murphy Oil Corporation and consolidated subsidiaries, which includes a noncontrolling interest (NCI) in MP Gulf of Mexico, LLC (MP GOM). The filings consolidate MP GOM; the earnings releases state headline metrics excluding NCI unless noted. This split recurs in every consumer assessment. The pack contains no separate issuer-only, borrower-only or guarantor-only statements.

### Reader summary

The debt, cash flow and liquidity statements are complete through the third quarter of 2026. | Medium | No indentures, credit agreement, ratings or earnings presentations are supplied, so debt terms and covenants rest on filing summaries. |

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports a credit snapshot for MURPHY OIL CORP with limitations, and no consumer is blocked. The reasoning runs from evidence to source risk to consequence. Evidence: the audited FY2025 10-K and the Q3 2026 10-Q carry complete balance sheets, operations statements, cash-flow statements, a note-level debt schedule, a lease maturity table, a segment note and a liquidity paragraph, and the Q3 release adds non-GAAP reconciliations. Source risk: all debt terms, guarantee structure and covenant levels are read from summaries inside filings, because the indentures and the credit agreement are only listed as exhibits incorporated by reference and are not in the pack; the filings do not report credit ratings; and the 2042 notes coupon differs between two filings. Consequence: the debt-structure, liquidity and coverage consumers can proceed on filed figures, but each must carry the covenant, coupon and perimeter limitations forward, and none may present covenant headroom or instrument-level seniority as verified. The assessment is source sufficiency only and CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED: it does not assert normalized quarters, reconciliation, or acceptance of any downstream input.

Strongest contrary evidence: the Q3 2026 release and the Q3 10-Q describe different perimeters for the same quarter (production including versus excluding NCI), and the Q3 10-Q segment note shows 2025 comparative revenue that differs slightly from its own statement of operations. Neither blocks use; both require a perimeter label on every figure.

## Calculations

These are consistency checks used to establish whether sources tie. They are not normalized outputs and are not handed on as analytical results. Inputs are thousands of US dollars from the cited pages unless stated.

1. Notes payable tie, September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:13): 117,582 + 600,000 + 500,000 + 339,761 = 1,557,343, which equals the printed total notes payable of 1,557,343. Less unamortized debt issuance cost and discount of 17,712 gives 1,539,631, equal to the printed 1,539,631.

2. Total debt tie (page:13-14): 1,539,631 + finance lease obligations 94,721 = 1,634,352, equal to the printed total debt including current maturities. Balance sheet (page:2): 11,229 + 1,623,123 = 1,634,352. Ties. The revolver balance is nil at September 30, 2026 and 100,000 at December 31, 2025 (page:14).

3. December 31, 2025 notes tie (10-K page:112): 78,899 + 148,590 + 117,582 + 600,000 + 339,761 = 1,284,832, equal to the printed total. The 10-K principal repayable schedule (page:113: nil in 2026, 78.9 million in 2027, 148.6 million in 2028, 217.6 million in 2029, nil in 2030, 939.8 million thereafter, in dollars of millions) sums to 78.9 + 148.6 + 217.6 + 939.8 = 1,384.9 million dollars, versus 1,284.8 million dollars of notes plus the 100.0 million dollar revolver draw at that date = 1,384.8 million dollars; the 0.1 million dollar difference is rounding. The 10-K contractual obligations table prints 1,384.8 million dollars of debt excluding finance leases and interest (page:73).

4. Weighted-average coupon test for the 2042 notes (principal-weighted, on the four tranches outstanding at September 30, 2026; the release gives 6.3 percent, release 2026-11-04 page:2). Using 6.375%: (117,582 × 7.050 + 600,000 × 6.000 + 500,000 × 6.500 + 339,761 × 6.375) ÷ 1,557,343 = (828,953 + 3,600,000 + 3,250,000 + 2,165,976) ÷ 1,557,343 = 9,844,929 ÷ 1,557,343 = 6.32 percent, which rounds to 6.3. Using 5.875% for the 2042 notes: (828,953 + 3,600,000 + 3,250,000 + 1,996,096) ÷ 1,557,343 = 9,675,049 ÷ 1,557,343 = 6.21 percent, which rounds to 6.2. The release figure therefore matches the 6.375% label. This supports, but does not prove, that 6.375% is the current coupon; the cause of the change is not supplied.

5. Liquidity inputs (10-Q Q3 page:47; page:14): cash and cash equivalents 500.3 million dollars; Amended RCF commitment 2.0 billion dollars; borrowings nil; letters of credit 0.4 million dollars. Undrawn capacity net of letters of credit = 2,000.0 − 0.4 = 1,999.6 million dollars; plus cash 500.3 = 2,499.9 million dollars, consistent with "approximately 2.5 billion" and the release's 2.50 billion dollars. Not a liquidity analysis: no minimum cash, expiring facility or restricted cash review is done here. The cash figure includes NCI (release page:2) and 105.1 million dollars held outside the United States (10-Q Q3 page:47).
6. Perimeter bridge for Q3 2026 production (release 2026-11-04 page:13): 192,283 − 5,788 = 186,495 BOE per day, equal to the printed excluding-NCI figure.

7. Segment-to-statement difference for 2025 comparatives (10-Q Q3 page:29, page:30 versus page:3): three months, 733.2 − 732.985 = 0.2 million dollars; nine months, 2,096.7 − 2,094.266 = 2.4 million dollars (rounded to one decimal). 2026: 854.9 versus 854.974 and 2,516.8 versus 2,516.833, equal within rounding.

8. Net debt as printed by management (release 2026-11-04 page:10-11): total debt 1,634.3 − cash 500.3 = 1,134.0 million dollars at September 30, 2026; 1,385.0 − 377.2 = 1,007.8 million dollars at December 31, 2025. Both tie. This management measure includes the revolver draw at year-end 2025 and is stated including NCI cash.

Issuer: MURPHY OIL CORP (issuer id mur; ticker MUR; registrant "Murphy Oil Corporation and consolidated subsidiaries"). As-of date and cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Current period q3-2026 (three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026); prior period fy-2025 (year ended December 31, 2025). Reporting currency: USD; the filings state thousands of US dollars and the narrative and non-GAAP tables state millions. All figures in this handoff are US dollars. Nothing dated after 2026-11-05 is used as fact.

Task: the financial base for the credit snapshot. It sets out the reported statement lines, the separately labelled calculation bridges (EBITDA, last-twelve-months, leverage, interest cover, liquidity, maturities), the debt stack and claims outside debt, the covenant position as far as the sources allow, the latest quarter and subsequent events, and the gaps. It is an intermediate handoff for the next modules, not the final report.
Perimeter and periods, applied to every figure below:

- Perimeter: Murphy Oil Corporation consolidated, which includes 100 percent of MP Gulf of Mexico, LLC (MP GOM) with a 20 percent noncontrolling interest (NCI) (EX-99.1 2026-11-04 page:6). The filings and the calculations in this handoff are consolidated, including NCI. The earnings releases state headline and non-GAAP measures excluding NCI; where a release figure is used it is labelled ex-NCI. Debt and cash are consolidated; the release states that its cash is inclusive of NCI (EX-99.1 2026-11-04 page:2).

- Periods: Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 are the three-month periods ended March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026; 9M 2026 and 9M 2025 are the nine months ended September 30; FY2025 and FY2024 are calendar years; LTM Q3 2026 is the twelve months ended September 30, 2026, calculated as FY2025 less 9M 2025 plus 9M 2026. A fourth quarter 2025 is not printed and appears only inside the LTM calculation.

- Carried from the CP-0 handoff: no indentures or credit agreement, no ratings, no earnings presentation, an unresolved coupon label on the 2042 notes, the NCI perimeter split, no discrete fourth quarter 2025 and no interim cash taxes. This handoff re-tests each against the sources before relying on it.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage is low and liquidity is ample: total debt is 0.89x calculated EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, with 2,499.9 million dollars of cash and undrawn revolver. Heavy exploration and development spending keeps free cash flow modest. | Medium | EBITDA is our own calculation including the noncontrolling interest; covenant definitions, indentures and ratings are not in the sources, so headroom and instrument terms are unverified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt rose to 1,634.4 million dollars from 1,385.1 million dollars at year-end 2025, after a new notes issue and a new finance lease. | Leverage still fell because calculated EBITDA rose faster, and no note matures before May 2029. | High |

| Operating cash flow of 1,517.6 million dollars for nine months 2026 was largely absorbed by 1,333.0 million dollars of property additions and dry hole costs. | Free cash flow after dividends of 150.5 million dollars is thin, so distributions and exploration depend on commodity prices. | Medium |

| Liquidity is cash of 500.3 million dollars plus 1,999.6 million dollars undrawn on a revolver that matures in January 2031. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; revolver covenants are known only from the previous facility's description. | Medium |

| Interest cover is 21.29x on interest paid for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 15.82x for FY2025. | Cash interest of 86.3 million dollars is below interest expense of 100.9 million dollars; cover on expense is 18.22x. | Medium |

| The 2042 notes show a 5.875% coupon in the annual report and 6.375% in the third quarter report, and filings include the 20 percent noncontrolling interest while releases exclude it. | Match perimeter before comparing figures; the coupon on 339.8 million dollars of notes needs the indenture. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is sufficient for a credit snapshot of MURPHY OIL CORP, with stated restrictions. Evidence: the audited FY2025 statements and the unaudited Q1 to Q3 2026 statements are complete and tie to the debt note (total debt 1,634.4 million dollars at September 30, 2026 equals current maturities of 11.229 plus long-term debt of 1,623.123 million dollars). Calculated EBITDA (operating income plus DD&A plus impairment, consolidated) is 1,837.5 million dollars for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 against 1,394.0 million dollars for FY2025, so total debt over EBITDA is 0.89x against 0.99x and net debt over EBITDA is 0.62x against 0.72x even though debt rose by 249.3 million dollars. Mechanism: revenue from production rose in the nine months (2,507.9 against 2,076.8 million dollars) on higher realized prices while ex-NCI volumes fell (176,620 against 182,585 BOEPD), and lease operating expenses fell from 605.0 to 436.4 million dollars; the 2025 comparison also carries a 115.0 million dollar impairment that the calculation adds back. Management's own ex-NCI adjusted EBITDA gives a close cross-check: 1,784.8 million dollars for the same twelve months, or 0.92x total debt. Source risk and consequence: the strength of the leverage and cover ratios rests on a high price period and a calculated, NCI-inclusive EBITDA; the free cash flow cushion is small because property additions and dry hole costs of 1,333.0 million dollars absorb most of the 1,517.6 million dollars of operating cash flow, and the balance sheet carries claims outside the debt figure (operating leases, asset retirement obligations, pension and retiree medical, commitments). The metrics therefore support a view of low financial leverage with good near-term liquidity and no note maturity until May 2029, but not a view of covenant headroom, instrument seniority or guarantor coverage, which the sources cannot verify.

EBITDAX = EBITDA + exploration expenses, including undeveloped lease amortization. These are not the management definitions, which start from net income attributable to Murphy, exclude NCI, add back accretion and remove foreign exchange and derivative items (EX-99.1 2026-11-04 page:9-10).
- LTM Q3 2026 = FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025, applied to each flow line.
- Total debt = total debt including current maturities (notes net of discount plus finance leases) plus the revolver draw. Net debt = total debt less cash and cash equivalents.
- Free cash flow (calculated) = net cash provided by continuing operations activities less property additions and dry hole costs, without removing working capital changes and including NCI.

### Reader summary

### Business and transaction view

MURPHY OIL CORP is an independent, publicly listed oil and gas exploration and production company with no sponsor, no controlling owner identified in the sources and no acquisition or leveraged transaction driving the credit view. The decision drivers are therefore the operating model and recent change, not transaction structure. Evidence: crude oil and condensate is 86.1 percent of nine-month 2026 revenue from production, no commodity derivative contracts were in place at September 30, 2026, and realized prices rose sharply on the year (for example United States onshore crude at 86.48 dollars per barrel in Q3 2026 against 65.48 dollars in Q3 2025) while total hydrocarbon production fell 7 percent in Q3 2026 and 3 percent in nine months 2026, which management attributes mainly to lower Gulf of America volumes (natural decline) and to the timing of new onshore wells (10-Q Q3 page:34-36). Risk mechanic: an oil-weighted, unhedged revenue base converts price moves almost directly into cash flow, so the 2026 earnings recovery is a price result with lower volumes; sustaining production requires continuing capital in decline-prone Gulf of America fields (about half of nine-month revenue is United States offshore) while the company also funds exploration and appraisal in Côte d'Ivoire, Vietnam and the Gulf of America. Credit implication: leverage and liquidity are currently strong (CP-1 handoff), but they depend on commodity prices and on management choosing to keep exploration and shareholder returns within cash flow; the sources show that discretion being exercised conservatively on buybacks and with a refinancing that extended maturities, but they do not show the covenant or indenture limits that would constrain distributions or new debt. Credit-relevant change in the period: the January 2026 refinancing (500.0 million dollars of 6.500% notes due 2034, 227.5 million dollars of 2027 and 2028 notes redeemed, revolver upsized to 2.0 billion dollars and extended to January 2031), the first oil at Lac Da Vang in Vietnam with an 83.9 million dollar finance lease for its floating storage vessel, raised 2026 production guidance, and an October 2026 drillship agreement worth approximately 225 million to 325 million dollars gross. The view is limited by missing ownership percentages, customer concentration and capital allocation plan terms (see Gaps).

### Credit view

MURPHY OIL CORP is a financially conservative but price-exposed oil producer, and its credit is sound today. The strongest support is low leverage (total debt of USD 1,634.4 million is 0.89x calculated last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million), liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million and no note maturing before May 2029. The weakest point is that crude oil supplies 86.1 percent of revenue with no commodity derivatives in place, while exploration, development and a new drillship commitment absorb most operating cash flow, leaving little after dividends. What decides the outcome is the oil price and management's willingness to cut discretionary spending and buybacks when it falls; the covenant and indenture limits that would bound that discretion are not in the sources.
### Credit assessment

Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium, below High because CP-1A judges this module ready only with limitations and because covenants, indentures, ratings, ownership and customer concentration are missing. Basis: [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; Chart data: leverage, interest cover, liquidity, debt maturities; Debt stack] and [CP-1A Business and transaction view; Credit translations; Consumer readiness].

Rationale. Evidence: MURPHY OIL CORP has total debt of USD 1,634.4 million, net debt of USD 1,134.1 million, cash of USD 500.3 million, calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million, interest paid of USD 86.3 million and cash plus undrawn committed capacity of USD 2,499.9 million, with the nearest note maturity in May 2029 [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: those figures come from a period when United States onshore crude realized USD 86.48 per barrel in Q3 2026 against USD 65.48 in Q3 2025, on an unhedged, oil-weighted revenue base whose volumes fell 7 percent in Q3 2026 [CP-1A Company and operating model: Pricing; Hedging; Volume and mix]. Credit implication: near-term default risk is low on the reported figures, because leverage, liquidity and the maturity profile give a large buffer; the risk sits in how the company behaves if prices fall, which depends on contract terms the sources do not provide.
### Credit thesis

Category: Analyst Interpretation. MURPHY OIL CORP is a low-leverage, well-funded but oil-price-exposed producer whose creditworthiness depends on keeping discretionary spending and shareholder returns inside cash flow. Basis: [CP-1 Financial base view] and [CP-1A Governance, capital allocation and disclosure behaviour].
### Key findings

First, the company's leverage is low and has fallen even though debt rose. Total debt was USD 1,385.1 million at December 31, 2025 and USD 1,634.4 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 249.3 million from a USD 500.0 million notes issue, a USD 83.9 million finance lease and the repayment of USD 227.5 million of notes and the USD 100.0 million revolver draw, while calculated EBITDA rose from USD 1,394.0 million (FY2025) to USD 1,837.5 million (LTM Q3 2026), so total debt over EBITDA moved from 0.99x to 0.89x [CP-1 Debt stack; Chart data: leverage]. The management-basis cross-check gives 0.92x on adjusted EBITDA attributable to Murphy of USD 1,784.8 million.

Second, the improvement is a price result. Revenue from production rose to USD 2,507.9 million for nine months 2026 from USD 2,076.8 million, with realized prices up about a third and production down 3 percent, and lease operating costs fell on lower Gulf of America workovers, which management itself describes as partly offset by activity elsewhere [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model: Cost structure; Management explanation of costs]. Part of the cost gain may not repeat, and none of the price gain is protected, because crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and there were no commodity derivatives at September 30, 2026.

Third, free cash flow is modest. Calculated free cash flow (operating cash flow less property additions and dry hole costs) was USD 184.6 million for nine months 2026, which after USD 150.5 million of dividends and USD 21.2 million of distributions to the minority holder of MP Gulf of Mexico, LLC leaves USD 12.9 million; management's own adjusted free cash flow was negative USD 32.2 million for the same period, excluding the minority share [CP-1 Free cash flow and shareholder distributions]. Cash still rose by USD 123.1 million because operating cash flow exceeded investing outflow by USD 155.9 million, while financing used USD 32.8 million.

Fourth, maturities and liquidity are comfortable. No note matures until May 2029 (USD 117.6 million), followed by USD 600.0 million in October 2032, USD 500.0 million in February 2034 and USD 339.8 million in December 2042; the USD 2.0 billion revolver matures January 2, 2031 and is undrawn apart from USD 0.4 million of letters of credit [CP-1 Chart data: debt maturities; Liquidity]. The 2026 refinancing moved the company from a revolver and shorter notes to this profile.

Fifth, claims outside the debt figure are large. Asset retirement obligations are USD 1,065.4 million, operating lease liabilities USD 653.8 million, and net pension and retiree medical liabilities were USD 195.8 million at December 31, 2025, before commitments of USD 1,648.0 million at that date and a new drillship agreement of about USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross from the first quarter of 2027 [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Adding the first three to total debt gives USD 3,549.3 million, or 1.93x calculated LTM EBITDA (see Calculations).

Sixth, creditor protections are unverified. The previous revolver's tests were a maximum leverage ratio of 3.25x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.50x before an investment grade ratings date, and a 60 percent maximum debt to total capitalization after it; the amended facility's terms, the indentures and the ratings are not supplied, and which test applies is unknown [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; CP-0 Gaps]. The mechanical distance to the stated levels is wide (see Calculations) but is not covenant headroom.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Low leverage is a documentary result: total debt is USD 1,634.4 million against calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million, and net debt is 0.62x (Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the characterisation) [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 2,499.9 million of cash and undrawn capacity, a revolver to January 2031 and no note before May 2029 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity; Chart data: debt maturities]. Operating cash flow was USD 1,517.6 million for nine months 2026, 52.0 percent above nine months 2025, and calculated LTM EBITDA covers interest paid 21.29x (Documentary Fact for the cash flow, Analyst Interpretation for the cover) [CP-1 Calculations]. Asset base: proved reserves of 730.0 million barrels of oil equivalent at December 31, 2025, about 10.6 years of 2025 production, spread across Eagle Ford Shale, Gulf of America, Tupper Montney, Kaybob Duvernay, Canada offshore and Vietnam, with 43 percent undeveloped (Documentary Fact for reserves, Analyst Interpretation for diversification) [CP-1A Company and operating model: United States assets; Canada assets; Reserves and replacement]. Capital allocation flexibility: buybacks fell from USD 301.4 million in 2024 to USD 102.6 million in 2025 and USD 0.8 million in nine months 2026, which favors creditors, and no related-party leakage, creditor-adverse transaction or sponsor is documented (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading) [CP-1A Governance, capital allocation and disclosure behaviour]. Disclosure quality: quarterly reconciliations of non-GAAP measures and a covenant compliance statement each quarter (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance].

Weaknesses. Unhedged oil exposure: crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and no commodity derivatives were in place at September 30, 2026; a 10 percent lower oil price on nine-month volumes would have cut revenue and EBITDA by about USD 215.9 million, or 14.0 percent of nine-month calculated EBITDA, before any cost offset (Documentary Fact for the exposure, Analyst Interpretation for the arithmetic) [CP-1A Hedging; Revenue streams]. Thin cash cushion after investment and dividends, as described above (Documentary Fact for the amounts) [CP-1 Free cash flow]. Concentration and decline: United States offshore supplies 50.2 percent of nine-month revenue, and production including the minority share fell 7 percent in Q3 2026, mostly on Gulf of America volumes (Documentary Fact for the percentages, Management Language for the cause) [CP-1A Geographic revenue mix; Volume and mix]. Discretionary, high-risk spending: exploration expense was USD 155.2 million for nine months 2026, including USD 86.7 million of unsuccessful well costs, and the drillship agreement adds a contracted element from 2027 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Cost structure; Transaction summary]. Claims outside debt, including asset retirement obligations equal to about 65 percent of total debt (Analyst Interpretation, calculated) [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Unverified creditor terms: covenants, indentures, ratings, ownership percentages and customer concentration are missing (Insufficient Information; each missing datapoint is listed under Gaps) [CP-0 Gaps; CP-1A Gaps]. Perimeter: the minority holder takes a share of Gulf of America cash flow, 13.5 percent of consolidated nine-month 2026 net income, and releases and filings use different perimeters (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model: MP GOM subsidiary].

| Operating and environmental incidents | August 2026 produced water release at Tupper Montney West, amount not stated; abandonment and remediation costs raised other operating expense | Recurring cost with unquantified tail; monitored | Minor | [CP-1A Operating incidents] |
## Calculations
Inputs are from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs unless a source is named; EBITDA means the calculated, consolidated figure defined in the CP-1 handoff (operating income plus DD&A plus impairment).

1. Illustrative oil price sensitivity (arithmetic, not a forecast): nine-month 2026 crude oil and condensate revenue of USD 2,158.6 million (CP-1A, from 10-Q Q3 page:8-9) times 10 percent = USD 215.9 million; divided by nine-month 2026 calculated EBITDA of USD 1,537.3 million = 14.0 percent. It assumes constant volumes, no cost or royalty offset and no tax effect.

2. Mechanical distance to the previous facility's stated levels (not covenant headroom): total debt USD 1,634.4 million divided by 3.25 = USD 502.9 million, so calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million could fall by 72.6 percent before total debt over EBITDA reached 3.25x; interest paid of USD 86.3 million times 2.50 = USD 215.8 million, so EBITDA could fall by 88.3 percent before EBITDA over interest paid reached 2.50x. The covenant definitions are not supplied.

3. Claims-inclusive leverage (illustrative): total debt USD 1,634.352 million + operating lease liabilities USD 653.756 million (September 30, 2026) + asset retirement obligations USD 1,065.394 million (September 30, 2026) + pension and retiree medical net liabilities USD 195.814 million (USD 132.415 million + USD 63.399 million, December 31, 2025) = USD 3,549.316 million; divided by USD 1,837.474 million = 1.93x. It mixes dates, treats asset retirement obligations as debt-like although they are costs of operations, and excludes commitments and letters of credit. Asset retirement obligations over total debt: 1,065.394 / 1,634.352 = 65.2 percent.

4. Cash walk, nine months 2026 (USD million, 10-Q Q3 page:4-5): operating cash flow 1,517.609 - investing outflow 1,361.686 = 155.923; less financing outflow 32.834, plus exchange effect 0.016 = 123.105, equal to the increase in cash from 377.196 to 500.301.
5. Free cash flow after distributions, nine months 2026 (CP-1): 184.570 - 150.528 - 21.164 = 12.878, shown as USD 12.9 million.
6. Interest cost sensitivity of the 2042 notes coupon: 339.761 million times 0.5 percentage points = USD 1.7 million a year (1,698.8 thousand).

7. Figures carried unchanged from CP-1 and CP-1A, recomputed here as a check: total debt 1,634.352 / EBITDA 1,837.474 = 0.89x; net debt 1,134.051 / 1,837.474 = 0.62x; EBITDA 1,837.474 / interest paid 86.305 = 21.29x; liquidity 500.301 + 1,999.6 = 2,499.9; operating cash flow growth 1,517.609 / 998.162 - 1 = 52.0 percent.
